title: Who Was Declared, Who Was Deported: the Passive with Ser

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the passive with *ser* + past participle from B1 Unit 18: *La ley fue aprobada por el Parlamento*. The participle agrees with the subject, and *por* names who did the action. The history of Belize is full of things that were done to a place or a people, so it is a good place to use it.

sections.title: Ser + participle, agreeing with the subject
rows: La barrera de coral fue declarada Patrimonio de la Humanidad.
feminine singular: the barrier reef was declared a World Heritage Site
Los garífunas fueron deportados por los británicos.
masculine plural: the Garifuna were deported by the British
La música garífuna fue proclamada obra maestra por la UNESCO.
El criollo es hablado por muchos beliceños.
present tense: Creole is spoken by many Belizeans

items.spanish: La barrera de coral fue declarada Patrimonio de la Humanidad en 1996.
items.english: The barrier reef was declared a World Heritage Site in 1996.

items.spanish: Los garífunas fueron deportados por los británicos a la isla de Roatán en 1797.
items.english: The Garifuna were deported by the British to the island of Roatán in 1797.

items.spanish: La música garífuna fue proclamada obra maestra por la UNESCO en 2001.
items.english: Garifuna music was proclaimed a masterpiece by UNESCO in 2001.

items.spanish: Las lenguas mayas son habladas por muchas familias del sur.
items.english: The Maya languages are spoken by many families in the south.

sections.content: Use *ser* + participle when you want to name the doer or stress the result; with *se* (B1 Unit 6) you leave the doer out. Do not change *por* into *de* or *para*: *deportados por los británicos*. And remember the agreement: *declarada* goes with *barrera*, *deportados* with *garífunas*.
